newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso still firm on rates cut hope.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso still firm on rates cut hope.

text.p: The Mexican peso retained virtually all of its initial advance against the dollar at mid-morning dealing on Friday on expectations domestic rates could continue to decline, dealers said.
"Many investors think Mexico is doing well, a trader said. "They think rates can come down more, so they tie that in with the exchange rate."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart stood 4.4 and 3.9 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.7730/7.7760 and 7.7700/7.7730 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile closed trade for the day 5.8 centavos firmer at 7.7610/7.7650 per dollar.
